competitors.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google Search/Network, YouTube, Android, Chrome, Google Cloud, Gemini)
competitors.why: Named in the 10-K (Item 1A): Google integrated competitive products with Android and proposed phasing out third-party cookies in Chrome; the 10-Q of 2026-10-22 names YouTube as an industry peer. It is the largest competitor for the same advertiser budgets (Google advertising 81.6 billion USD in Q2 2026 against META advertising 59.4 billion), for user time (YouTube ads, Shorts against Reels) and in frontier AI models (10-K Item 1 names frontier AI development as a competing field; Google Cloud revenue +82% in Q2 2026 and +103% in Q3 2026 on enterprise AI).

competitors.why: Named in the 10-K (Item 1A) as a competitive product that has reduced some users' engagement with META's products, and in the 10-Q of 2026-10-22 as an industry peer (with YouTube) whose adoption of teen protections conditions about 5.3 billion USD of META's contingent settlement payments; short-video and ad competitor for the same users and advertisers. metrics.basis: private company; no revenue, margin or user figure from a primary or attributed source was retrieved

bottlenecks.reading: The scarce, capital-heavy input of the whole competitive set is AI compute and data-center capacity, and each rival adds it with its own balance sheet. META guides 2026 capital expenditures (including finance-lease principal) to 135-145 billion USD (narrowed from 130-145), spent 34.9 billion in Q3 2026 against operating cash flow of 32.8 billion (free cash flow negative 2.1 billion), and says it is still developing 2027 capacity plans. Alphabet's last-twelve-month capex is 132.4 billion with Q2 2026 free cash flow negative 5.9 billion; Amazon's purchases of property and equipment are 173.0 billion over twelve months (free cash flow negative 7.6 billion). How long compute stays scarce is not evidenced by an industry source in this lane; what the filings show is that funding it already exceeds operating cash flow at META, Alphabet and Amazon.

META's growth in the latest quarter comes from yield per ad impression, not from users: in Q3 2026 ad impressions rose 10% and the average price per ad 14% while family daily active people rose only 3% (3.64 billion). The scarce thing META sells is measurable, AI-ranked attention in saturated markets; management attributes the gain to AI-driven engagement, recommendations and monetization (a management statement, not independently measured). Like-for-like rivals are user-constrained too: Snap North America DAU fell 7% and Pinterest U.S. and Canada MAU grew 4% in Q2 2026, so the ad-dollar gains of Snap (+19%) and Pinterest (+18%) also rest on pricing and ARPU.

Distribution and ad signals are controlled by two competitors: Apple (iOS data-use changes and Safari limit ad targeting and measurement while Apple expands its own advertising business) and Google (Android integration of competing products, Chrome cookie policy). The 10-K treats this as structural and ongoing, and the dependency has no capacity-addition date: it can only be hedged by owning more first-party signal and engagement.

Paid adoption of META's next-platform hardware is not yet visible in its own numbers: Reality Labs revenue was 1.276 billion USD in the first nine months of 2026 against 1.252 billion a year earlier (Q3 2026: 443 million against 470 million) with a Q3 operating loss of 4.129 billion; management expects 2026 Reality Labs losses of 18-19 billion USD and around 15 billion in 2027 as investment is reallocated to AI. Apple's wearables, home and accessories line alone was 7.9 billion USD in its June 2026 quarter (+6.5%).

Competitors monetize frontier AI through paid consumption, META through advertising yield: Google Cloud revenue grew 82% to 24.8 billion USD in Q2 2026 and AWS grew 37% (Amazon also booked 53.4 billion of other income mainly from its Anthropic investments), while META reports no AI-model or cloud revenue line (Family of Apps other revenue, which holds WhatsApp paid messaging and subscriptions, was 1.1 billion USD in Q3 2026). META launched its first frontier model (Muse and Muse Wonder) in Q3 2026 per management; whether it produces paid adoption outside ads is not evidenced yet.

notes: fd NAMED COMPETITORS (10-K Item 1 / 1A, pf_10k_20260129): Item 1 'Competition' names NO company (it describes companies providing connection, sharing, discovery and communication products, companies selling advertising, frontier-AI developers and consumer hardware / AR-VR developers). Item 1A names TikTok (competitive products that have reduced some users' engagement), Apple and Google (each integrated competitive products with iOS and Android; Apple's iOS and Safari changes limit ad targeting and measurement while it expands its own advertising business; Google proposed phasing out Chrome third-party cookies). The 10-Q of 2026-10-22 (pf_10q_20261022) names YouTube and TikTok as industry peers. Frontier-AI, consumer-hardware and AR/VR rivals are not named in any META filing.

fd PEER SET (analyst choice, stated): GOOGL, AAPL and TIKTOK are the 10-K's named competitors; AMZN, SNAP and PINS are NOT named in the 10-K and are added because they sell the same advertiser budgets or ad-funded user time and publish their own numbers (reason in each why). TikTok is private: no numbers. OpenAI and Anthropic (frontier AI) are private and not examined; Microsoft was not examined.

fd SHARE MARKET (attributed, EMarketer as reported, search excerpt, original not read, fd_emarketer_2026): worldwide net ad revenue 2026 forecast META about 243.5 billion USD (growth 24.1% after 22.1% in 2025, share of digital ad spend 26.8%) against Google about 239.5 billion (growth 11.9%, share 26.4%), Amazon 82.1 billion (about 9%); the three together 62.3% of worldwide digital ad spend in 2026 against 59.9% in 2025. EMarketer's forecast was completed before the court rulings against Meta and YouTube. A forecast, not a measured share. The reported Google figure varies by outlet (one cites 229.4 billion for Google and YouTube combined), so the scope is uncertain.

fd SHARE USERS: META family daily active people 3.64 billion in September 2026 (+3% year over year), ad impressions +10%, average price per ad +14% in Q3 2026 (pf_rel_20261021_1). Snap DAU 493 million (+5%, North America 92 million, -7%); Pinterest MAU 640 million (+11%, U.S. and Canada 106 million, +4%) in Q2 2026. Engagement share against TikTok and YouTube cannot be measured: TikTok is private and YouTube's usage is not disclosed; the 10-K itself says TikTok has reduced some users' engagement.

fd SHARE HARDWARE AND AI (hypothesis, not a measured share): in Reality Labs, META is flat in revenue (9M 2026 1.276 billion USD against 1.252 billion) while Apple's wearables, home and accessories revenue is 7.9 billion USD a quarter; in AI-model monetization Alphabet (Cloud +82%) and Amazon (AWS +37%) show paid consumption that META does not report. Both are readings of different scopes, labelled as hypotheses for the analyst.

fd YOUTH-SAFETY CROSS-LINK (pf_10q_20261022): about 5.3 billion USD of the 18.59 billion USD multistate settlement (about 30%) becomes payable state by state only if peers such as YouTube and TikTok adopt teen protections and each peer with annual profits above 10 billion USD agrees to pay the same amount; as of 2026-09-30 these conditions were not met. The 10-Q also warns that if YouTube, TikTok or others do not adopt the same measures META may experience disproportionate adverse user-engagement impacts from its product changes: a competitive-disadvantage risk for the analyst (key risk candidate), not a number.

fd MARGINS AND CAPEX CONTEXT (derived, TTM to June 2026): operating margin META is for gather_numbers; competitors GOOGL 33.1%, AAPL 33.2%, AMZN 12.1%, PINS 4.9%, SNAP -5.1%.
